rationale: Base ordinary hours pay is the core qualifying earnings case
Casual loading on ordinary hours counts in full regardless of the percentage
Shift penalties for ordinary hours worked count
Workers compensation paid for hours actually worked counts
Flexi-time is treated as ordinary hours, unlike a rostered day off or time off in lieu
A payment for a missed rest or meal break where the employee keeps working ordinary hours counts
Charge rates paid to a contractor for outcomes achieved count under the expanded contractor definition
A public holiday paid at the ordinary rate when not worked counts
Paid annual leave taken during employment counts
Leave loading demonstrably linked to a lost opportunity to work overtime is the one excluded case
Long service leave paid directly by the employer, not through a portable scheme, counts
Long service leave paid by a scheme administrator under a portable scheme is excluded, the opposite outcome to the same leave paid in-house
Family and domestic violence leave counts, an easy category to overlook
A rostered day off taken and paid at ordinary rates counts
Time off in lieu of overtime, taken and paid at ordinary rates, counts, unlike cashing it out
Paid study leave counts
Special paid leave, including compassionate leave, counts
Gardening leave, keeping an employee on the payroll during a notice period without requiring work, counts
Employer paid parental leave is excluded
Government paid parental leave is excluded even when the employer merely administers the payment
Community service leave, including volunteer emergency service activities, is excluded
Jury duty leave is excluded
Defence reserve leave for Australian Defence Force volunteers is excluded
Cashing out annual leave while still employed counts
Cashing out sick, personal or carers leave while still employed counts
Cashing out a rostered day off while still employed counts
Unused annual leave or leave loading paid on a normal termination is excluded
Unused long service leave paid on a normal termination is excluded
An hourly on-call allowance for ordinary hours of work counts, unlike an on-call allowance for hours outside ordinary hours
An allowance for adverse working conditions such as a confined space counts
A flat meal allowance paid regardless of whether the expense was incurred counts, unlike a true reimbursement
An overtime meal allowance paid with the reasonable expectation it will be spent on the meal is excluded
A call back allowance is treated as an overtime-related payment and excluded, despite the allowance naming
All commission payments count
Commission counts even when earned entirely outside ordinary hours, one of the actual Payday Super changes
A performance bonus for ordinary hours work counts
A bonus labelled ex gratia still counts if it is paid for ordinary hours work, the label does not change the category
A return to work bonus paid after parental leave counts
A bonus paid solely for work entirely outside ordinary hours is excluded, the opposite outcome to the same scenario paid as a commission
Remuneration paid to a non-working director still counts
A bonus paid to end industrial action and resume work counts, a niche return to work payment category
A bonus paid to an employee who withdraws a resignation counts
Unused leave and leave loading paid on termination is excluded, regardless of the reason for termination
Unused personal or carers leave paid on termination is excluded
Salary sacrificed to superannuation counts if the underlying payment would otherwise have been qualifying earnings
Salary sacrificed to superannuation is excluded if the underlying payment, such as overtime, would not otherwise have been qualifying earnings
Could be annual leave taken in service, which counts, or unused leave paid on termination, which is excluded, the name alone does not say which
Could be an ordinary hours performance bonus, which counts, or a bonus solely for work outside ordinary hours, which is excluded, the name alone does not distinguish these
Could be compensation for hours actually worked, which counts, or payment while not required to work, which is excluded, the name alone does not say which
Could be an expense allowance expected to be fully spent, which is excluded, or a flat allowance paid regardless of the expense incurred, which counts, the name alone does not distinguish these
